title: Dynamic per-lane INT8/FP8 throttler and KV window propagation to reduce tail latency
author: Ibrahim Noor
release_notes: Adaptive per-lane throttler and KV shared-window propagation reduce tail latency for mixed INT8/FP8 workloads. Backwards compatible; feature gated.
description:
Context: production traces showed intermittent tail-latency spikes when serving mixed quantized variants (INT8 baseline with FP8 fallbacks) under continuous-batching. Root cause: imbalance between scheduling lanes where early-arriving requests warmed KV cache and later lanes incurred repeated dequant/scale passes, amplifying GEMM latency and creating hot tails. Motivation: restore predictable latency SLOs without disabling quantized fastpaths or adding global serialization.

What this PR does: implements a dynamic per-lane throttler and a KV shared-window propagation mechanism plus small kernel-level fuses to eliminate an extra dequant pass in the common path. Key components: (1) scheduler: per-lane token budget and adaptive slack calculation (lane throttler) that temporarily delays tokens from the fastest lanes to improve alignment and KV locality; (2) KV cache: windowed propagation so that a warmed prefix from one lane is opportunistically exposed to nearby lanes within a small time/sequence window, reducing redundant cache loads; (3) kernels: new hybrid-quant microkernel that fuses smoothquant scale application into the GEMM prolog for INT8->FP32 accum paths, avoiding a separate dequant broadcast; (4) continuous batching: request metadata includes lane affinity hinting so the runtime groups requests likely to share KV prefixes.

Design notes and trade-offs: the lane throttler is adaptive and conservative by default: it targets 95th percentile tail improvements with a small throughput impact (<1–3%) in microbenchmarks. The KV window uses a compact bloom-like prefix hint to avoid copying large prefixes — conservative conservative memory overhead and remains optional via runtime flag. Kernel fusion prioritizes correctness; we added code paths for FP32 accumulation to avoid precision regressions on edge models.

Compatibility and toggles: all features are behind config flags and a runtime feature gate (env REDWOOD_FEATURE_LANE_THROTTLER / REDWOOD_FEATURE_KV_WINDOW). Fallback to previous behavior on any assertion or if perf regressions exceed thresholds. No surface API changes.

Testing and validation: unit tests for scheduler heuristics, KV window correctness tests, and kernel unit smoke tests were added. End-to-end microbenchmarks measured on c6g-gpu-class clusters show 18–34% reduction in p99 latency for mixed INT8/FP8 chat workloads (p50 unchanged). Additional stress tests run for 48h to verify stability.

Checklist: [x] scheduler + throttler implementation; [x] KV shared-window; [x] fused kernel path and safety fallbacks; [x] unit and integration tests; [x] perf benchmarks and reporting; [x] docs note.

Related: ENG-4129 (lane-scheduling), ENG-4190 (quant-kernel optimizations).
